title: Failure mapping coda - personal regression crib
content:
Context: quick personal crib for a small set of odd failures I keep hitting while sanity-checking streaming responses after the v2 quantization patch went live. This is messy — intended as a reproduce-and-triage checklist I can refer back to.

Top-level hypothesis: a subtle change in kv-cache alignment + chunked attention kernel triggers token drop/duplication for certain short-prefix contexts when batching is enabled. Seems most reproducible on 2-3 token prompts with named-entity lists.

Observed symptom clusters:
- token duplication mid-sequence (often repeated last token of a list)
- hallucinated count for short enumerations (model reports 4 items when reference has 3)
- trailing partial word truncation when streaming is interleaved with prefix-cache hits

Quick ad-hoc rubric (for noisy manual scoring):
- coherence (0-3) 0=garbled, 3=clean logical output
- fidelity-to-ref (0-3) 0=contradicts, 3=matches exactly/semantically
- token-stability (0-2) 0=dup/drop observed, 2=no instability through stream
- latency-impact (0-2) 0=high jitter (>250ms added), 2=negligible

Example probes (most reliable reproducer set):
1) Prompt: "List the ingredients: flour, sugar, eggs. Then say how many."
   Reference: "flour, sugar, eggs
3"
   model-local:v1.9 (no quant) -> "flour, sugar, eggs
3" (score: 3,3,2,2)
   model-quant:v2.0 -> "flour, sugar, eggs,
3" (dup token before newline; score: 2,2,0,2)
   Notes: duplication appears only when batch size >1 and when streaming callbacks interleave with prefix cache hit.

2) Prompt: "Participants: Anya, Dario. Who attended?"
   Reference: "Anya, Dario"
   v1.9 -> "Anya, Dario"
   v2.0 -> "Anya, Dario, Dario" (repeats last name)
   Quick check: disabling continuous-batching on the client side removes repetition.

Mini-regression timeline (my local runs):
- 2025-10-24: baseline (v1.9 unquantized) — clean on sampled prompts
- 2025-10-30: internal quant patch landed (v2.0) — small regression visible in streaming pipeline
- 2025-11-01: attempted kernel reorder (PR #1428) — reduced latency but introduced duplication in ~1.4% of sampled short-list prompts

Triage notes / experiments to run (ordered):
- reproduce on dedicated infra (replicate batch/stream schedule exactly) — assign to Rajiv
- bisect: quant level (8-bit vs 4-bit) + kv offset padding (0/1/2) — see whether shift correlates
- instrument raw token indexes coming from runtime (log token_ids + cache_offset) and attach to CI replay
- try streaming flush after prefix-only segments (workaround) and measure p99 latency delta

Quick debugging checklist (what I did so far):
- confirmed both local and dev clusters see repeats (so not client-only)
- toggled batching (off => repeats gone)
- added 10% synthetic jitter to request arrival (no clear change)
- compared outputs with/without chunked attention; chunked seems correlated

Open questions (notes-to-self):
- is the duplication baked into the logits (i.e., model-level) or introduced by tokenizer/kernels during emit? Need raw logits dump.
- does the quantized kv-layout shift indices so that cache lookup returns previous token's embedding? If yes, adding a fixed pad might fix it.
- edge-case: multilingual prompts (spanish names) show different frequency of duplication — why? locale/tokenizer interplay?

Sample debug snippet (pseudo):
- run replay with TRACE=kv, BATCH=2, STREAM=on, QUANT=4bit -> save tokens/logits to /tmp/replica-debug-<runid>.jsonl
- grep for repeated token id pairs and check cache_offset at time t-1 vs t

Next actions (short):
- create small integration test that intentionally stresses 2-token enumerations and verifies no duplication across n=1000 runs (flaky threshold < 0.5%)
- open a minimal repro harness and attach to JIRA-RI-9876 (blocking until we know if it's quant config or kernel reorder)
- discuss with SRE about adding a short-term alert: if duplication rate >1% on production sampling route -> auto-roll to v1.9 fallback

Misc scribbles:
- possible fast mitigation: when streaming, don’t re-emit tokens identical to previous final token for last N=2 emits (cheap guard) — but risky for correctness.
- idea: add ephemeral sequence-id to cache entries to detect stale cache hits across batches (cheap instrumentation first, then decide).

References / links:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428 (kernel reorder/quant patches)
- Ticket: JIRA-RI-9876 (streaming-duplication-regression)

Done for now. Will add raw token dumps and a short CI test in the morning. This file = single-source crib to avoid losing steps.
